problemStatement.formal:
Let $c_1,c_2>0$. Is it true that, for any sufficiently large $x$, there exist more than $c_1\log x$ many consecutive primes $\leq x$ such that the difference between any two is $>c_2$?



This is well-known if $c_1$ is sufficiently small.

knowledge.progressSummary: AXIOM ELIMINATION: Proved conjecture_implies_run_growth (formerly axiom). Reduced axiom count from 4 to 3. Proof uses le_csSup with BddAbove bound from strict monotonicity of prime enumeration.
insights: conjecture_implies_run_growth is a structural consequence of definitions, not a deep number-theoretic result
Key insight: the set {k | exists run of k primes <= x with gaps > c} is BddAbove by x+1, since n <= nthPrime(n) by strict monotonicity
Transfer from Filter.Eventually on R to N uses Archimedean property (exists_nat_ge)
Remaining 3 axioms are genuinely deep: erdos_partial_result (second moment method), average_gap_grows (PNT consequence), prime_number_theorem_asymptotic (PNT itself)

prime_number_theorem_asymptotic requires PNT in Mathlib (not currently available in v4.26.0)
